name: Prowler
what: An open-source cloud security and compliance scanner with hundreds of checks across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. It can run as a CLI, SDK or self-hosted stack and maps findings to common frameworks.
when: For recurring configuration reviews of cloud accounts you own, CI pipelines, and purple-team validation after hardening Identity, storage, logging and network controls.
cost_note: Open-source CLI/SDK/self-hosted are free; Prowler also offers commercial cloud products.
example: Install the CLI per the current docs (pip or container) on a jump host with read-only cloud credentials.
Run a provider scan for an approved Azure subscription or AWS account and write JSON/HTML output.
Filter to identity, storage and logging checks first; open tickets for failed high findings with the check ID from the report.
Re-run on a schedule and track the trend instead of treating one scan as a one-off audit.
pitfalls: Scanner credentials need broad read access; lock them to the assessment principal and rotate after use.
Checks can produce false positives around intentional exceptions; verify before remediating production.
Multi-cloud setups need separate provider configuration; do not assume AWS flags apply to Azure.
